Matchbook Learning Morning Meeting · K–2 Behavior Toolkit · Belly Breathing07

Slide 1 · Title & Promise R2

Put one hand on your belly. “Our belly can be like a balloon. When we breathe in slow, it gets big. When we breathe out slow, it gets small. Slow breaths help our body feel calm.” Say together: “My belly is a balloon!”

Look for

  • Eyes on the slide or on you
  • Hands on bellies
  • Students repeat the line

If it breaks

  • If students puff their cheeks or blow loudly: “Slow and quiet. Like a balloon floating, not popping.” Model once and move on.

Support adult

  • Sit beside any student who has had a hard morning

Language support

  • Touch your belly as you say “belly”
  • Spanish: barriga, respirar · Kreyòl: vant, respire

Engagement move Equity stick: pull one name. “Show me where your belly is.” Pointing is a full answer.

Belly breathing is a body skill. Students learn it best when they are already calm, so practice it every day, not only when someone is upset.

Slide 2 · Regulate · Get Calm First R1

Model the gesture with them every time. “Smell the flower. Blow out the candle. Long and slow. Three times.” Do it with the class, not from the front.

Look for

  • Exhale longer than inhale
  • Shoulders drop
  • Gesture copied

If it breaks

  • If silliness: model silently once, then invite them back.

Support adult

  • Breathe audibly beside any student who cannot settle

Language support

  • No language demand; gesture carries it
  • Same two gestures used in every K–2 lesson

Engagement move LiveSchool: award a point to a student who breathes all three times with you. Name the behavior: “You breathed slow three times.”

Tell the class: “Today we learn one more way to breathe slow. It lives in our belly.”

Slide 3 · Orient · The Story R2, R3

Point to each picture as you tell it. “It was clean-up time, but Tee’s drawing was not done. His heart went fast. His shoulders got tight. His breath got short and quick. Tee put his hand on his belly. He breathed in slow, and his belly got big, like a balloon. He breathed out slow, and his belly got small. He did it three times. His body felt calm. Then he asked, ‘Can I finish my drawing later?’ His teacher said, ‘Yes. Thank you for asking calmly.’” Then have the class say together: “Hand on belly. Breathe in slow. Breathe out slow. Three times.”

Look for

  • Students follow the pictures in order
  • Whole class repeats the We say line

If it breaks

  • If students giggle at “belly”: smile and keep going. “Yes, belly! Everyone has one.”

Support adult

  • Point to each panel as the teacher narrates

Language support

  • Four pictures, two words each; numbers carry the order
  • Show “busy body” by lifting your shoulders up tight, then dropping them

Engagement move Equity stick: “Which picture shows Tee’s belly getting big? Point.” Pointing is a full answer.

Tee did not have to stop feeling upset. He calmed his body first. Then he could use his words.

Slide 4 · Connect · Turn and Talk R3, R4

Show knee to knee with a student partner. “Turn knee to knee. Look at Tee. His body feels busy. Tell your partner: Tee can ___.” Give 30 seconds, then ring back. Ask one pair: “What did your partner say?”

Look for

  • Partners face each other
  • Students name belly breathing or point to a picture
  • Some students name another calm tool

If it breaks

  • If a pair is stuck: kneel in and say the stem with them.
  • If partners argue: “Take turns. You go first, then you.”

Support adult

  • Pair any student who needs support with a steady partner before the lesson starts

Language support

  • Pointing to a picture is a complete answer
  • Spanish: “Tee puede respirar despacio” · Kreyòl: “Tee ka respire dousman”

Engagement move Equity stick: call two names to share. Every calm tool on the slide is a right answer.

All three pictures are good choices. Belly breathing is the one we practice today.

Slide 5 · Practice · Watch Me, Then Show Me R3, R4, R5

Invite one student to the front to model with you. “Hand on belly. Breathe in through your nose, slow, slow, slow. Feel your belly get big. Now breathe out slow, like you are blowing a balloon away. Feel your belly get small.” The student model does it once while the class watches. Then the whole class does three belly breaths together, counting with fingers: one, two, three.

Look for

  • Hands on bellies
  • Bellies move out on the breath in
  • Breath out is slow and quiet

If it breaks

  • Excellent model: “Show us again. Everyone, watch the hand on the belly move.”
  • Partly right model: “Your breath was slow. Now put your hand on your belly so you can feel it.”
  • Silly model: “Thank you. Let’s see it the calm way.” Call a new student; no commentary.

Support adult

  • Kneel beside a student who lifts their shoulders instead of their belly. Place your own hand on your belly and breathe together.

Language support

  • Four step pictures with words; students can point instead of naming
  • Spanish: Inhalo, exhalo · Kreyòl: Respire antre, respire soti

Engagement move LiveSchool: award the student model a point. Name it out loud: “You breathed slow, and your belly got big.”

If a student does not feel their belly move, have them lie on their back later with a stuffed animal on their belly and watch it ride up and down.

Slide 6 · Commit · My Promise Today R2, R5

Put your hand on your heart. “Say it with me: I can breathe slow to calm my body.” Then: “When your body feels busy, what can you do? Point to one.” Model it first: “I can belly breathe.”

Look for

  • Every student says the promise
  • Every student points to one picture

If it breaks

  • If a student does not choose: offer two pictures and let them point.

Support adult

  • Remind any student who points to the calm corner that belly breathing works there too

Language support

  • Hand on heart carries the promise
  • Spanish: Puedo respirar despacio · Kreyòl: Mwen ka respire dousman

Engagement move Equity stick: pull three names: “Which one did you point to?” Pointing counts.

Slide 7 · Transition · How We Leave R1, R4, R5

“How we leave is how we start our learning. One belly breath first. Now: stand up. Calm body. Walk. Ready to learn.” Do not time this at K–2.

Look for

  • Calm bodies while moving
  • Calm walking, not rushing

If it breaks

  • “Let’s try that again. Back to your spot.” Rebuild clean, no commentary on individuals.

Support adult

  • Stand at the destination, not behind the group

Language support

  • Four icons, four words
  • No timing pressure at this age

Engagement move LiveSchool: award a point to the table that walks with calm bodies the whole way.

Use one belly breath before every transition this week. Say: “Balloon belly, then we move.”
